facts.text: Commerce sprang to life in 1872 when merchants William Jernigan and Josiah Jackson opened a trading post that became the town’s downtown.
The town earned its name, Commerce, from the bustling cotton trade that flourished between the Middle and South Sulphur rivers.
East Texas A&M University relocated to Commerce after its original campus burned down in 1894, cementing the city’s academic roots.
Commerce earned the title Bois d'Arc Capital of Texas because it sits in the geographic heart of the tree’s historic range.
Within Commerce’s limits stands “Big Max,” the second‑largest bois d'arc tree in Texas, a living monument to the region’s natural heritage.
A railroad reached Commerce in 1874, linking it to Fort Worth and sparking a boom that shaped the town’s early growth.
